evidence.reason: The stale-worktree removal path relies on non-forced `git worktree remove` to refuse removal, but Git's cleanliness/status check excludes ignored files. So a stale checkout with clean tracked files, no unpushed commits, and an ignored local file is removed successfully, deleting that content without ever invoking `onStaleRefresh`. The same removal pattern at line 782 has the same gap. This is a data-loss defect in the existing stale-tree guard, not a request to enlarge contract scope; an ignored-file/ownership check before removal (or routing through the stale-refresh refusal path) is the small compatible fix.
